record.field: AI: Get Menu Details
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_get_menu_details(menu_ids)

**Tool Name: get_menu_details**
Retrieves detailed information (context, domain, search_view) for specific menus. MUST be called before using any open_menu_* tool to get menu-specific details.
Returns CSV with pipe (|) delimiter: ``` menu_id|model_name|context|domain|search_view 389|sale.order|{"search_default_my_quotation": 1}|[]|<search><fields>...</fields></search> 172|account.move|{"search_default_draft": 1}|[["type", "=", "out_invoice"]]|<search>...</search> ```
Key information: - Context: Default filters/groupings applied when menu opens - Domain: Permanent filters that cannot be removed by users - Search_view: Full XML structure with available filters, groupbys, and searchable fields
💡 Performance tip: Request multiple menu details in one call when comparing options ⚠️ Always validate the returned model matches your expectations
AI: Get Fields
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_get_fields(model_name, include_description)

**Tool Name: get_fields**
Lists ONLY searchable fields for a single model that can be used in domain filters. Essential for building valid domains - if a field isn't listed here, it CANNOT be used.
Returns format: ``` field_name|display_name|type|sortable|description partner_id|Customer|many2one(res.partner)|true|Customer for this order date_order|Order Date|datetime|true|Date when order was placed order_line|Order Lines|one2many(sale.order.line)|false|Lines in this order ```
Key points: - ⚠️ Only returns SEARCHABLE fields - others cannot be used in domains - For relationships: Shows related model in parentheses (many2one, one2many, many2many) - Only relationship fields can be used to traverse to other models - Literal fields such as char/text/float CANNOT be used for traversal - 'sortable' indicates if field can be used in order_by parameter
💡 Performance tip: When exploring multiple models, call this tool multiple times in ONE message Example: Exploring sale.order, product.product, and res.partner? Make 3 parallel calls.
AI: Open Menu List
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_open_menu_list(menu_id, model_name, selected_filters, selected_groupbys, search, custom_domain)

**Tool Name: open_menu_list**
Opens a list (table) view using search view elements. Best for: "Show me", "List all", detailed record viewing, sorting data.
Key features: - Apply multiple filters by name (from menu's search view) - Group records by available fields - Search within specific fields for text - Displays records in sortable table format - Ideal for reviewing, filtering, and exporting data
💡 Use search parameter to filter by any searchable field BEFORE considering custom domains ⚠️ Use only filter names and groupby fields from menu data ⚠️ Each search string must use format 'field=text'. Array can contain multiple search strings or be empty []

**Tool Name: open_menu_kanban**
Opens a kanban (card-based) view using search view elements. Best for: Stage/status visualization, pipeline views, workflow management.
Key features: - Display records as cards in columns - Apply filters from menu's available options - Group by workflow stages or other fields - Search within specific fields - Ideal for CRM pipelines, task boards, project workflows
⚠️ Use only filter names and groupby fields from menu data ⚠️ Each search string must use format 'field=text'. Array can contain multiple search strings or be empty []
AI: Open Menu Pivot
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_open_menu_pivot(menu_id, model_name, selected_filters, row_groupbys, col_groupbys, measures, search, custom_domain)

**Tool Name: open_menu_pivot**
Opens a pivot table with advanced search and filtering. Best for: "Top N" queries, rankings, cross-tabulation, performance metrics.
Key features: - Supports filters from search view - Groups data by rows AND columns simultaneously - Aggregates measures (sum, avg, count) - Supports text search across searchable fields - Excel-like pivot table functionality
💡 ALWAYS call compute_report_measures() first to get valid measures 💡 For rankings: Include ordering in measures (e.g., ["amount_total desc"]) 💡 Use search parameter to filter by any searchable field BEFORE considering custom domains ⚠️ Prefer "Reporting" app menus for best pivot experience ⚠️ Each search string must use format 'field=text'. Array can contain multiple search strings or be empty [] ⚠️ Note: Uses row_groupbys/col_groupbys (arrays) instead of selected_groupbys
Example: For "top salespeople selling office products": - Use search=["categ_id", "office"] if categ_id is searchable - Only use custom_domain if no searchable field matches your needs
AI: Open Menu Graph
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_open_menu_graph( menu_id, model_name, selected_filters, selected_groupbys, measure, mode, order, search, stacked, cumulated, custom_domain)

**Tool Name: open_menu_graph**
Opens a graph/chart view using search view elements. Best for: Trends, comparisons, distributions, visual KPIs.
Supported chart types: - 'bar': Compare values across categories - 'line': Show trends over time - 'pie': Display proportions of a whole
Features: - Apply filters from menu's available options - Visualize a single measure - Group by one field for the chart axis - Search within specific fields - Stacking and cumulation options - Order control (ASC/DESC)
💡 Call compute_report_measures() first to find valid measures ⚠️ Each search string must use format 'field=text'. Array can contain multiple search strings or be empty [] ⚠️ Mode must be exactly 'bar', 'line', or 'pie' ⚠️ Order must be exactly 'ASC' or 'DESC'
AI: Compute Report Measures
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_compute_report_measures(menu_id, model_name)

**Tool Name: compute_report_measures**
Lists numeric fields (measures) available for aggregation in pivot/graph views. MUST be called before using measures in open_menu_pivot() or open_menu_graph().
Returns CSV with pipe (|) delimiter: ``` field_name|display_name|type|aggregator|sortable __count|Count|integer||true amount_total|Total|monetary|sum|true margin|Margin|float|sum|true quantity|Quantity|float|sum|true ```
Key points: - __count is always available (counts records) - Only numeric fields with aggregators are returned - Use field_name in measures parameter - For rankings in pivot: Add ordering (e.g., "amount_total desc") - Call multiple times in parallel if comparing different menus
